lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: By Pluto, Aeacus, give me the grand tour. Show me everything in the underworld.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: "Everything" is a tall order, Menippus. But I can hit the highlights. You already know Cerberus, and you met the ferryman who brought you over, and you saw the lake and the river of fire on your way in.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Yes, yes, I know all that, and I know you're the gatekeeper. I've seen the king, I've seen the Furies. I want to see the people. The ancients. Especially the celebrities.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Well, this one here is Agamemnon. This is Achilles. Idomeneus is right next to him, then Odysseus, then Ajax, Diomedes, and the rest of the great Greek heroes.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: [whistles] Oh, Homer... So much for the grand heroes of your epics. Just tossed on the ground, shapeless, unrecognizable. Nothing but dust and nonsense. Truly "strengthless heads." Anyway, Aeacus, who's this one?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: That's Cyrus. This one's Croesus, the one beyond him is Sardanapalus, the one past them is Midas, and that over there is Xerxes.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That's Xerxes? [laughs] Greece was terrified of you, you piece of trash? Just because you bridged the Hellespont and tried to sail through a mountain? And look at Croesus! Oh, Aeacus, please let me smack Sardanapalus on the jaw.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Absolutely not. You'd shatter his skull. It's incredibly effete.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Fine, but I'm at least going to spit on the little hermaphrodite.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Would you like me to show you the philosophers?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Oh, god yes.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Right. Well, first up, here is Pythagoras.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Hello, Euphorbus! Or Apollo, or whatever you're calling yourself these days.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: Greetings to you too, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: What happened to the golden thigh? You don't seem to have it anymore.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: No, I don't. Listen, let me look in your knapsack. Do you have anything to eat?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Just beans, my good man. So, nothing you can eat.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: Just give me the beans! The dead have different doctrines. I've learned that down here, eating beans is not, in fact, the same as eating your parents' heads.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Moving on... This is Solon, and that's Thales, and next to them is Pittacus, and the rest. All seven of the sages, as you can see.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: They're the only ones not moping, Aeacus. Quite cheerful, actually. But who's the one covered in ash, like a loaf of bread baked in the embers? The one completely covered in blisters?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: That's Empedocles, Menippus. Arrived half-baked from Mount Etna.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Ah, my excellent bronze-slippered friend! Whatever possessed you to throw yourself into a volcano?

lines.speaker: Empedocles
lines.text: [sighs] A bout of melancholy, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: [laughs] Melancholy? Please. It was sheer vanity, pretension, and a head full of hot air. That's what charred you to a crisp, right down to your bronze slippers—which you entirely deserved. Not that the stunt even worked. They found out you were dead anyway. Speaking of which, Aeacus, where in the world is Socrates?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: He's usually over there, talking nonsense with Nestor and Palamedes.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Still, I'd like to see him, if he's around.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: See the bald guy?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: They're all bald. That doesn't exactly narrow it down.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: I mean the snub-nosed one.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Same problem. They're all snub-nosed now.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Are you looking for me, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Exactly the man, Socrates.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: How are things in Athens?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Oh, lots of the young men say they're doing philosophy now. And if you just judge by their outfits and their dramatic pacing... they're absolute masters of the craft.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: I've seen plenty of those.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Yes, well, I imagine you've seen how your own students turned out. Aristippus showed up reeking of expensive perfume, and Plato arrived perfectly trained in sucking up to Sicilian tyrants.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: What do they think of me, though?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're a lucky man on that front, Socrates. Everyone thinks you were absolutely marvelous. They think you knew everything—which is funny, considering, well, to be entirely honest, you didn't know a damn thing.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: [chuckles] I told them that myself! They just thought I was being ironic.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And who are these boys around you?

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: This is Charmides, Menippus. And Phaedrus. And the son of Cleinias.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Good for you, Socrates! Even down here, keeping up the old trade. Never passing up a pretty face.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: What else could I do that's half as pleasant? Come, recline next to us, if you like.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, thanks. I'm going to go set up camp right next to Croesus and Sardanapalus. Listening to them wail about everything they've lost is going to be incredibly funny.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: I should be going as well. Can't have any dead slipping past the gates unnoticed. I'll show you the rest some other time, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Off you go. This was plenty for one day, Aeacus.
